question: A pole stands vertically on the ground with the help of a 12-metre steel wire tied to its top and affixed on the ground. If the steel wire makes an angle of 30º with the horizontal ground, then the height of the pole is equal to:
solution:
**Given:**

A pole stands vertically on the ground with the help of a 12-metre steel wire tied to its top and affixed on the ground. The steel wire makes an angle of 30º with the horizontal ground.

**Formula used:**

In a right triangle, height (h) = hypotenuse (H) × sin(angle)

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3d36d5dc2ec1e15f7dcc2be98588bdcb5ddbb320fb093caccd53b1f8dfcc930a.png] 

Height of the pole (h) = 12 × sin(30º)

⇒ h = 12 × 1/2

⇒ h = 6 meters

**∴ The correct answer is option (1).**
